## Why

A sliver is a small item carved from a slice, linked by parent, so a cheaper model can implement it (glossary.md:154). design.md:185 says slivers run as their own items under the cap. No cap is enforced today: the caps are only fields (registry.go:75,89) and launchRun has no check. Cap enforcement is S05.

From S10 (carried here from S08): split-part and sliver prompts need the same 'no handoff before review' wording as the implementer prompt.

## Implement

Owner decisions 2026-10-28 (interactive): slivers run as one chain: `ork run PARENT --slivers` runs the parent's slivers (items whose Parent is the slice, Item.Parent) one after another in the parent's worktree and branch and lands once at the end (record 124, slicer landing.md:29-31); a sliver is also startable alone with `ork run SLIVER_ID`, which queues behind a running parent run through the worktree guard. Tests first; re-anchor line numbers from the code. 1. Plan: list the slivers in order (slicer's order for the parent), their rows (RecommendRoles with the sliver condition, matrix rules u6-u9: a sliver that fails its gate twice moves to the next model up), and the single landing; the owner confirms the chain as one plan. 2. Engine: one worktree; each sliver is its own relay round set (implement, review, gate, finish) recorded as its own ledger run or as a child run of the chain run (decide in the implementation from what `slicer relay-run begin` accepts for several items and note it in the report); a sliver stopping stops the chain and keeps the branch for a retry from that sliver. 3. Caps: the chain counts as one run against the project and global caps (S05 is done: use its admission); a lone sliver counts as one. 4. TUI: the Overview and Running rows show the parent and the sliver position (2 of 4); the run tree nests slivers. 5. Correct design.md:185 ('their own items') to this chain model; glossary.md:154.
